title: Ust'-Ishim man, an early Siberian genome
summary: 45,000-year-old remains from western Siberia gave one of the oldest modern human genomes (2014). Its Neanderthal DNA segments dated human-Neanderthal mating to about 52,000-58,000 years ago; 2024 genomes narrowed this to 49,000-45,000.
why: The length of Neanderthal DNA chunks works like a clock for when interbreeding happened.

notes.problem: 'Later revised' is not in the cited page; name the revision and its source (2024 Ranis/Zlaty kun genomes, see HC-SCI-C2024-01).
